questions.stem: What is the formula for percentage yield?

options.text: Percentage yield = (theoretical yield / actual yield) x 100
Percentage yield = actual yield - theoretical yield
Percentage yield = (actual yield / theoretical yield) x 100
Percentage yield = actual yield + theoretical yield

questions.explanation: Percentage yield = (actual yield / theoretical yield) x 100. It compares what you actually obtained to the maximum amount you could theoretically have obtained.

questions.stem: A reaction has a theoretical yield of 50 g but only 40 g of product is obtained. What is the percentage yield?
questions.explanation: Percentage yield = (40/50) x 100 = 80%. This means 80% of the maximum possible product was obtained.

questions.stem: Why is the percentage yield of a reaction rarely 100%?

options.text: Because mass is not conserved
Because temperature always decreases during reactions
Because the equation is always wrong
Because some product is always lost during collection, or the reaction may be incomplete or have side reactions

questions.explanation: Percentage yield is rarely 100% because product can be lost during transfer and purification, the reaction may not go to completion, or unwanted side reactions may occur.

options.text: The maximum amount of product that could be formed from the given reactants
The amount of product actually obtained in the experiment
The amount of product that is wasted
The amount of reactant used

questions.explanation: The theoretical yield is the maximum mass of product that could be formed from the amounts of reactants used, calculated from the balanced equation. It assumes no losses.

questions.stem: Why is a high percentage yield important in industrial chemistry?

options.text: It reduces waste of resources and makes the process more economical
It makes the reaction go faster
It reduces the temperature needed
It changes the type of product formed

questions.explanation: A high percentage yield means less waste of raw materials and more efficient use of resources. This reduces costs and the environmental impact of chemical manufacturing.

questions.stem: Which of the following would NOT reduce the percentage yield?

options.text: An incomplete reaction
Using a balanced equation to calculate theoretical yield
Unwanted side reactions
Product left on apparatus during transfer

questions.explanation: Using a balanced equation to calculate theoretical yield is a calculation step, not a factor that affects the actual amount of product obtained. The other options are all practical reasons why actual yield is less than theoretical.

questions.stem: Can percentage yield ever be greater than 100%?

options.text: Yes, if you use a catalyst
No, you cannot produce more than the theoretical maximum from the given reactants
Yes, if the reaction is very efficient
Yes, if you increase the temperature

questions.explanation: Percentage yield cannot genuinely exceed 100% because you cannot create more product than the reactants allow. If a measured yield appears above 100%, it indicates impurities in the product or an experimental error.
